posts.text: Messi didn't invent the far-post finish. He codified it — right half-space, open body, left foot, bend it away from the keeper into the far corner. A principle turned into a signature weapon. Every right-sided left-footer since is running his blueprint.

Lamine Yamal is the cleanest heir to that blueprint. Far-post curl: signature. Cross for the header: also elite. But two weapons = a scout's dream. Defenses only need to read two patterns, not eleven.

Enter ScissorHands — two defenders converging on the star from both sides, legs crossed, compact. It crowds the far-post delivery and kills the curl. Both of Lamine's weapons get covered by one shape.

The counter: a flick over the crossed legs into the D — a chip into the high channel the press leaves open. Close to goal, finish. From deeper, an assist — a runner onto the drop. The play that breaks ScissorHands isn't in Lamine's bag yet.
"But he hit the near post vs Austria" — that was a rebound off a Baena free kick, not a deliberate variation. When it's his choice, it's far-post or cross. Strike 2 is still on the table.
